minor.issue: Legacy seeded products (seed-protetor, seed-refri, seed-salgadinho, seed-agua) are missing the 'in_stock' key in the response because startup seed uses $setOnInsert. New/toggled products carry the field. Frontend handles absence gracefully (treats as in-stock), but the API contract stated in the review is not uniform. Fix: on startup, run `db.products.update_many({'in_stock': {'$exists': False}}, {'$set': {'in_stock': True}})` alongside the existing seed upsert.

rca_of_issue: Root cause of the single failing backend assertion: seed startup uses `db.products.update_one(filter, {'$setOnInsert': p}, upsert=True)`. This only sets fields when the document is first created. Since seed products existed from earlier iterations (before in_stock was added to the model), the new key never propagates onto them. Reproduction: fresh DB has all fields, but any DB carried over from iter<9.1 misses in_stock for the 6 seed rows. Mitigation: (a) migrate legacy rows on startup with `update_many({'in_stock': {'$exists': False}}, {'$set': {'in_stock': True}})`; or (b) use `$set` selectively for the new field in the seed loop.
